column1: # docs/shim-ratchet.tsv -- the RATCHET CEILINGS for plan_shim.md §8's close.
# Every number here is a CEILING, recorded at the close of the shim project,
# and every one of them is re-measured FROM THE TREE on each test run. The
# tests that read this file are
#   sourcesharp/test/shim_vpc_stock_rows_test.cpp    the two stock-TU counts
#   sourcesharp/test/shim_reason_letters_test.cpp    the marker counts and size
# and they FAIL when a measured number goes ABOVE its ceiling. Going below is
# the whole point of the port and needs no ceremony beyond lowering the row.
# NOTHING HERE IS A KEEP-LIST. That distinction is the reason this file holds
# only counts. A list of file names nobody re-derives rots silently -- a row
# naming a file that was deleted three phases ago still reads as a claim, and a
# file nobody added to the list is invisible. Every row below names a SUBJECT
# the test re-walks, so a row whose subject has gone reddens rather than
# quietly describing a tree that no longer exists.
# HOW TO CHANGE IT
#   you made a number smaller   lower the row, in the same commit
#   you made a number BIGGER    that is the regression this file exists to
#                               catch. Raising a row is a deliberate act: say
#                               in the commit message what came back and why.
# MERGING TWO LANES' VERSIONS: do not keep both. Re-measure against the merged
# tree and write the number you measured -- two lanes each lowering one row and
# a keep-both resolution leaves a row that was never true of any tree.
# columns:
# metric
# The stock-TU counts. plan_shim.md Phase 2's exit condition was zero stock
# sources in the SERVER -- met, and pinned here so it stays met. The client's
# stock TUs are the port's remaining native surface and are counted the same
# way; the server's zero would be a vacuous pass if the count had stopped
# matching, so the client's non-zero count is the positive control as well as
# a ceiling. A stock TU is one under game/ or public/, except
# public/tier0/memoverride.cpp, which every Source DLL links.
